subject: physics_2
question_text: Three capacitors of capacitances 1 μF, 2 μF and 3 μF are connected in parallel. (a) What is the ratio of charges? (b) What is the ratio of potential differences?

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Two structural checks are IMPOSSIBLE for this paper: the two-book union check (the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only) and the past-paper back-test (the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers). Hand-checked: in parallel V is common, Q = CV so Q ∝ C, giving 1 : 2 : 3; V ratio 1 : 1 : 1 — the book's answers are correct.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Ratio of charges
lines: (a) In parallel the potential difference V is
the same across each capacitor. Q = CV, so
the charge divides in proportion to C:

lines.text: Q₁ : Q₂ : Q₃ = C₁ : C₂ : C₃ = 1 : 2 : 3

steps.margin_note: First mark. Name the common quantity (V), then Q ∝ C.
steps.why: Each capacitor sits directly across the same two terminals, so each takes the full applied V; with V fixed, Q = CV makes the charge proportional to the capacitance.
common_mistakes: Starting the ratio without stating that V is common — that one line is the working.
Writing the series result 1 : 1 : 1 for the charges.

recall.must_convey: That V is the same across each, so Q is proportional to C, giving 1 to 2 to 3.
reject: V ratio one to one to one

steps.memory_tip: Parallel: V common, so the charges copy the capacitances — 1 : 2 : 3.

steps.margin_note: Second mark. In parallel the potential differences are equal by connection.
steps.why: A potential difference is set by the two terminals a capacitor is joined between; in parallel all three share the same pair of terminals, so all three read the same V.
common_mistakes: Writing 6 : 3 : 2 here — that is the SERIES potential-difference ratio.

recall.must_convey: That in parallel every capacitor has the same potential difference, ratio one to one to one.

steps.memory_tip: Parallel means the same two terminals for all — one V for everyone.

insider_note: One line of reasoning per part: V common gives Q ∝ C. Bare ratios with no line of working risk the marks.
